tasks.title: Define DevLog product UX and information architecture
tasks.description: Design: Map the core user flows for DevLog: task list, create/edit/delete task, filter/sort controls, AI actions (prioritization, decomposition, status update, custom agent). Define the minimal information architecture and page layout for a single-user engineering task tracker. Include decisions for how AI outputs are presented (inline panel, modal, or side drawer), how task details are edited, and how to keep the UI simple and fast to scan. Deliver wireframe-level guidance and component hierarchy recommendations for the frontend scaffold.

tasks.title: Implement task data model, persistence, and CRUD API
tasks.description: BE: Build the backend data layer and REST API for tasks with required fields: title, description, status (todo / in-progress / done), priority (low / medium / high), createdAt. Implement create, read list, read single, update, and delete endpoints. Add persistence using a simple local storage approach suitable for the assignment (SQLite, JSON file, or equivalent), and document the choice and limitations. Ensure tasks persist across reloads and that API responses are normalized and validated. Include basic error handling for missing/invalid fields.

tasks.title: Build task list, filtering, sorting, and CRUD UI
tasks.description: FE: Scaffold the main DevLog interface in Next.js with a clean task list view, task creation/edit form, delete action, and task detail presentation. Implement filtering by status and sorting by priority or created date. Wire the UI to the backend API, manage loading/error states, and keep the interface minimal and usable. Ensure the frontend supports the required fields and reflects persistence after refresh. Use agent-assisted scaffolding for the initial component structure and styling, then refine manually where needed.

tasks.title: Create AI agent for task prioritization
tasks.description: BE/AI: Implement a multi-step agent that analyzes the current task list and recommends what to work on next, with a human-readable explanation of the reasoning. The agent must consider priority, task age, and status rather than simply returning the first item. Design the flow so it can inspect the full task context, rank candidates, and produce a concise recommendation plus rationale. If using an LLM, structure prompts and tool/context inputs so the behavior is agentic and not a single-shot generic response. Expose the result through an API endpoint for the frontend.

tasks.title: Create AI agent for task decomposition with clarification flow
tasks.description: BE/AI/FE: Implement an agent that takes a task title and description, generates a structured list of subtasks, and optionally creates them in the app. If the task is ambiguous, the agent should ask a clarifying question before generating subtasks. Define the backend orchestration for multi-step reasoning, the API contract for returning subtasks vs clarification requests, and the frontend interaction for reviewing and confirming generated subtasks before creation. Keep the output structured and actionable for engineering work.

tasks.title: Create AI agent for Slack-style status updates
tasks.description: BE/AI: Build an agent that generates a short asynchronous status update in a team Slack style based on a task, its subtasks, and/or notes about progress. The tone should adapt to the task context and be concise enough for internal communication. Implement an API endpoint that accepts task context and returns a polished update draft. Include guardrails so the output remains grounded in the provided task data and does not invent progress.

tasks.title: Add one custom agent feature for engineering workflow
tasks.description: BE/AI: Propose and implement one additional agentic feature that is genuinely useful for an engineering team. Examples could include risk detection for blocked tasks, duplicate-task detection, or a daily digest of stale/high-priority work. Choose one with clear product value and implement it as a multi-step agent that uses task context and produces an actionable output. Document why this feature matters for the team and what tradeoffs were made.

tasks.title: Generate agent-assisted UI scaffold and refine styling
tasks.description: FE/Design: Use an AI coding agent to scaffold the initial UI components, layout, and styling for DevLog, then manually polish the result. Focus on a clean, readable interface that supports the task list, filters, forms, and AI action panels. Record what was generated by the agent versus what was adjusted manually, and ensure the final UI is coherent and maintainable. This work should also inform the AGENT_LOG.md documentation.

tasks.title: Document architecture, setup, env vars, and agent workflow
tasks.description: BE/FE/QA: Write README.md with local setup instructions, architecture overview, persistence choice and limitations, and how to use each AI feature. Add .env.example with all required environment variables and no real secrets. Create AGENT_LOG.md describing which coding agents were used, what tasks they handled, where they helped, and where manual intervention or rewrites were needed. Include honest notes about compromises and any mocked AI behavior if applicable.

tasks.title: Verify end-to-end behavior and AI feature quality
tasks.description: QA: Test the full DevLog flow locally, including task CRUD, filtering/sorting, persistence after reload, and each AI endpoint/UI flow. Validate that the prioritization agent uses multiple factors, the decomposition agent can request clarification when needed, and the status update generator stays context-aware. Check error handling, empty states, and basic usability. Confirm npm install && npm run dev works cleanly and that README instructions are sufficient for a reviewer to run the app.
